extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants/owners, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners handling confidential/proprietary/protective-order materials and petitions to expunge
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and requirements for submitting, labeling, Office handling, and petitioning to expunge trade secret, proprietary, or protective-order materials in U.S. patent application, reissue, and reexamination files under MPEP §724 and 37 CFR 1.59. Covers what may be submitted under §724.02, how the Office treats such materials, timing, and petition content/processing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required labeling of submitted confidential/proprietary/protective-order materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Information considered trade secret, proprietary, or subject to a protective order must be clearly labeled and filed in a sealed, clearly labeled envelope or container. Each document or item must be clearly labeled as a “Trade Secret” document or item, a “Proprietary” document or item, or as an item or document “Subject To Protective Order.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the terms “Confidential,” “Secret,” “Restricted,” or “Restricted Data” to mark these documents (to avoid confusion with national security markings). If the item is “Subject to Protective Order,” the proceeding/tribunal must be set forth on each document or item. The envelope/container and each document must be labeled with complete identifying information (application/file destination, Office/area, TC Art Unit, Examiner, application number, filing date, title of invention, etc.). Examples of appropriate envelope labels are provided in MPEP §724.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and routing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential/proprietary/protective-order materials must be filed in a sealed, clearly labeled envelope or container and accompanied by a transmittal letter; such envelopes should be hand-carried to the Customer Window or mailed to the Commissioner for Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid mishandling, the envelope/container should be hand-carried to: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office Customer Service Window, Randolph Building, 401 Dulany Street, Alexandria, VA 22314. Alternatively mail to Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450. Each submission will be date-stamped and noted on the 'Contents' of the application/reexamination file; for Image File Wrapper (IFW) applications, the Office will place such envelopes in an Artifact folder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal letter content for confidential submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The transmittal letter must contain the same identifying information as the envelope/container and must state that the materials are considered trade secrets or proprietary, or are subject to a protective order, and are being submitted for consideration under MPEP §724.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transmittal letter should also state whether a petition under 37 CFR 1.59 and the fee (37 CFR 1.17(g)) to expunge the information, if found not to be material to patentability, accompanies the submission. The receipt of the transmittal letter and envelope/container will be noted in the application record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using §724.02 to submit information favorable to patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither 37 CFR 1.56 nor 1.555 require disclosure of information favorable to patentability, and such information should not be submitted in accordance with MPEP §724.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of information favorable to patentability that should not be submitted under §724.02 include evidence of commercial success of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office treatment: maintenance and sealing until materiality determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials submitted under MPEP §724.02 will be maintained in the original envelope/container and will not be publicly available until a determination has been made as to whether the information is 'material to patentability.' The face of the file will be notated to indicate presence and location of trade secret/proprietary/protective-order material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IFW processing, see IFW Manual; notation such as 'TRADE SECRET MATERIALS FILED WHICH ARE NOT OPEN TO PUBLIC' is sufficient. If materials are found to be material to patentability, they become part of the file history (and will be scanned for IFW) and become public upon issuance; if not material, they will be expunged if a petition to expunge is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement for filing a petition to expunge
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) to expunge must accompany the submission or be filed prior to certain prosecution milestones in order to avoid public release of submitted proprietary materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must be filed prior to the mailing of a notice of allowability or notice of abandonment for original and reissue applications, and prior to, or shortly after (in time to be addressed before the printing process), the mailing of a Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) for reexamination proceedings. If a petition is not timely filed, the materials may remain in the file and be open to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in a petition to expunge submitted under MPEP §724.02 (items A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) to expunge information submitted under MPEP §724.02 must include the fee (37 CFR 1.17(g)) and must contain certain statements and commitments to establish appropriateness of expungement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required elements: (A) a clear identification of the information to be expunged without disclosure of details; (B) a clear statement that the information is trade secret/proprietary/subject to protective order and not otherwise public; (C) a commitment to retain such information for the period of enforceability of any patent that issues; (D) a statement that the petition is submitted by or on behalf of the party in interest who originally submitted the information; (E) the fee per 37 CFR 1.17(g). Petitions should be directed to the Technology Center to which the application is assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for petitions to expunge unintentionally submitted information (items A–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to expunge information unintentionally submitted in an application (other than original disclosure) may be filed under 37 CFR 1.59(b) only if specific conditions are met and the petition fee is included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required findings/contents: (A) the Office can effect return prior to issuance of any patent on the application; (B) a statement that the information was unintentionally submitted and that failure to return it would cause irreparable harm to the submitting party or party in interest; (C) the information has not been made public; (D) commitment to retain information for the period of any patent that issues; (E) it is established to the satisfaction of the Director that the information is not material information under 37 CFR 1.56; (F) include the petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(g)). Untimely or deficient petitions may be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original disclosure exclusion and petition under 37 CFR 1.183
rubrics_metrics.description: Information forming part of the original disclosure (written specification including claims, drawings, and incorporated preliminary amendments) will not be expunged under 37 CFR 1.59 and requests to expunge such material must be filed under 37 CFR 1.183.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 1.183 must explain why justice requires waiver of the rules to permit expungement of original-disclosure material. Such petitions will ordinarily not be favorably entertained because original disclosures are scanned for record-keeping and changing the record may not be possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of confidential materials in reissue applications (37 CFR 1.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials submitted under MPEP §724.02 in a reissue application open to the public will be maintained separate and not publicly available until a materiality determination is made; if found material, they become part of the reissue file and open to public view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If protected material is found material, redaction may be possible to eliminate protected material while retaining important material; in that case, submit the redacted version and a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 requesting the unredacted version be sealed and replaced. If no petition to expunge is filed prior to notice of allowability/abandonment, materials will be available under 37 CFR 1.11(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of confidential materials in reexamination proceedings (37 CFR 1.11(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials properly submitted under MPEP §724.02 in reexamination will be sealed separate from the reexamination file and not publicly available until a materiality determination is made, provided a petition to expunge is timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to expunge should accompany the submission and be filed prior to, or in time to be addressed before, the reexamination proceeding's certificate printing process (NIRC). If petition is not filed timely, or is denied/dismissed, the materials will be released to the public with other reexamination papers. If portions are material and others not, petition may be dismissed but patent owner/requester given opportunity to separate material and non-material parts so non-material parts can be expunged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'material to patentability' (materiality standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Materiality is defined as any information which the examiner considers as being important to a determination of patentability of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner (or other appropriate Office official) is responsible for considering whether any portion or all of submitted information is material; if found material, petition to expunge will be denied and information becomes part of official file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of submissions mistakenly filed in incorrect application
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.59(b) covers situations where papers were unintentionally placed in an incorrect application file; a petition should request that the papers be expunged rather than transferred to the correct application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office can determine the correct application file from identifying information on the papers (e.g., application number, filing date, title, inventor name), the Office will transfer the papers to the correct file without need of a petition. The grant of a petition to expunge such papers will be governed by the same factors as unintentional submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing, notation, and recordkeeping by the Office for confidential submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt the transmittal letter and envelope/container will be date-stamped and brought to attention of the examiner; receipt will be noted on 'Contents' of the file and the face of the application/reexamination file will have notation indicating presence and location of trade secret/proprietary/protective-order material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IFW applications, the Office places the envelope in an Artifact folder and may scan materials if they become part of the file. Notations such as 'TRADE SECRET MATERIALS FILED WHICH ARE NOT OPEN TO PUBLIC' will be used; similar notations are used for proprietary or protective order materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition decision timing and abeyance during prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions on petitions to expunge are generally held in abeyance until prosecution is closed (allowance, mailing of Ex parte Quayle action, or abandonment), at which time a determination of materiality will be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While prosecution is open the examiner may not have finally considered what is material; petitioner may be so notified. If it is clear the information was submitted in the wrong application, the decision need not be held in abeyance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and obligations if petition to expunge is granted
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition under 37 CFR 1.59(b) is granted, the identified material is determined not to be material to examination and is removed from the official file; the petitioner must retain the expunged material for the life of any patent issuing from the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Technology Center Director decides such petitions only if information was submitted pursuant to MPEP §724.02 or in an information disclosure statement; petitions cannot be granted until application has been allowed or abandoned, or an Ex parte Quayle action has been mailed, except in certain circumstances.
